def: Information from a benchmark's test items reaching a model through its training data, so the score reflects recall instead of the ability being measured.
A unique marker placed in benchmark files so that honest data pipelines can exclude them and so a model's ability to complete it reveals exposure.
A contamination check that looks for long runs of consecutive words shared between a test item and training text.
Removing or flagging training documents that overlap with benchmark items before training.
Comparing a model's accuracy on original benchmark items with its accuracy on newly made equivalent items to reveal memorisation.
A black-box contamination test that checks whether a model assigns higher probability to a benchmark's published item order than to shuffled orders.
The state in which the best systems score so close to a benchmark's ceiling that differences among them are smaller than its noise.
The highest honest score on a benchmark given that some of its gold answers are wrong.
The loss of a benchmark's meaning over time as the world, the users and the systems it was written for change.
The observation that when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure.
A fixed part of a benchmark kept unchanged across versions so scores stay comparable while other items are refreshed.
Withdrawing a benchmark from claims and rankings, with its reason announced, its version archived and a successor named.
